speaker: Doctor
text: I understand you have been experiencing a headache and worsening vision over the past three weeks; to begin my evaluation, how severe is the headache on a scale of 1 to 10, and is it located on one side of your head or both? Additionally, do you experience any nausea, sensitivity to light, or changes in your vision such as blurriness, double vision, or loss of field?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Intracranial Malignancy (Brain Tumor).

I have reviewed your history of a 69-year-old female with a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision, with no constitutional symptoms like fever or weight loss; this clinical picture is highly concerning for a space-occupying lesion such as a glioblastoma or metastasis. Given the neurological decline, I am ordering an urgent MRI of the brain with contrast to visualize the lesion.
